title: GPU slice orchestration and speculative throttling controller
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a GPU slice orchestration layer plus a speculative throttling controller to improve tenant separation and reduce noisy-neighbor incidents on Dedicated capacity. The controller will make admission and preemption decisions using a short-term predictive model, progressive backpressure (speculative throttles), and slice reallocation heuristics. Goal: maintain per-tenant throughput guarantees with graceful degradation under bursty traffic while limiting tail latency regrowth for foreground tenants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New controller can enforce per-tenant throughput contracts across a 500-node simulated fleet with <5% SLA violations vs baseline under mixed synthetic workloads. 2) Noisy neighbor incidents (defined as >30% latency spike for other tenants) reduced by >=60% in chaos test. 3) Autoscale/Quota interactions documented and exercised in staging; rollbacks safe and automated. 4) Unit + integration tests cover admission, scoring, eviction, and slice reallocation logic. 5) Console shows per-tenant throttle signals and decision traces.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): build prototype admission/shaping service as a sidecar that ingests real-time metrics (QPS, token/sec, KV-cache hit rate, GPU occupancy) and emits throttle tokens. Phase 2: integrate with allocator to manipulate slices (soft shrink/expand) and implement speculative throttling policy (decay windows + probabilistic early-drop). Phase 3: CI tests, staging soak, performance tuning (kernel scheduling alignment). Phase 4: gradual rollout behind runtime-1.20 with canary -> 25% -> 50% -> global. Key PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9142, https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/2087.
migration_notes: Existing dedicated tenants will continue to run on current allocator until controller is enabled per region. Migration is opt-in per deployment; we will provide a migration tool to simulate speculative throttling in dry-run mode and produce KPIs for tenant owners. Important: preserve pinned-model semantics and manual hard-quotas during migration.
rollout_plan: 1) Dry-run in staging for 72h with synthetic spike schedule and recorded decisions. 2) Canary in us-west-2 on 5% of dedicated lanes for 48h with automated rollback on >2% increase in SLA violations. 3) Ramp to 25% for one week, then 50%, then full rollout with manual sign-off. 4) During ramp monitor: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput delta, cache hit-rate, eviction count, and tenant complaints.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: runtime/throttle-controller/decision-traces, runtime/tenant-isolation/eviction-stats. Alerts: SLO breach (p95 > target for two consecutive 5m windows), eviction-rate spike (+300% over baseline), speculative-throttle-drop-rate > 10%. Add a debug trace sampler to capture full decision context for alerts.
